title: Exclusive Behind the Scenes of the 2025 Game Light and Shadow: Expedition Team No. 33: How to Use Character Design to Tell a Story?
description: We are honored to invite Alan Reynaud, the chief character artist from Sandfall Interactive (the team behind "Light and Shadow: Expedition 33"), to unveil the captivating visual secrets behind this TGA Game of the Year nominee.

summary: ```# Exclusive Behind the Scenes of the 2025 Game "Light and Shadow: Expedition Team No. 33" ## Introduction My name is Alain Reynaud. I've been working at Soundfull for four and a half years now. I am the lead character artist there, primarily focusing on the main characters from the cast, as well as many enemies, bosses, a small amount of NPCs, and alternative skins. ## Game Overview **Expedition 33** is a turn-based RPG with real-time elements. During combat, players must parry and dodge enemy attacks while timing their own attacks to maximize power. The game is set in a French Belle Époque environment, rich with Art Deco themes. The narrative begins 67 years ago in the city of Lumière, where a massive monolith stands at the center. At the base of this monolith resides a paint dress that paints a number each year. Every individual matching the number written on the monolith disappears at that age. Each year, an expedition is launched to prevent the paint dress from committing the gommage and to save the world. The expedition is composed of characters like John, Mael, and Gustave, who endeavor to stop the paint dress. ## Character Design Process I contributed to the concept art, although the primary concept artist and art director for the project is Nicolas Maxon-Franconc. We worked closely together to develop the characters. Being a small studio allowed for more dynamic discussions about character design, enabling us to refine concepts collectively. ### Collaborative Workflow Our game director, Guillaume Broche, would provide us with a character script and descriptions. Nicolas would create initial concepts, and I would collaborate with him to refine them. This collaborative approach ensured that everyone had a comprehensive understanding of the project, fostering creativity. ## Artistic Inspirations Our inspiration largely stems from the Belle Époque period in France. We incorporated elements like classy suits for men and a vibrant color palette for the city of Lumière. Nicolas created drawings to serve as references, including Art Deco patterns that contributed to the visual style and color richness of the game environment. ## Marvelous Designer Techniques In terms of art direction, I approach character clothing design in **Marvelous Designer** with the aim of achieving a solid base. If I anticipate making significant changes in ZBrush, it defeats the purpose of using Marvelous. Instead, I focus on crafting garments that are as accurate as possible to ensure the main shapes and dynamics of the clothing are captured effectively. ### Character Clothing as Storytelling Each character's clothing communicates their personality. For instance, Ciel is portrayed with bright, asymmetrical clothing reflecting her vibrant yet challenging life. In contrast, Lune's symmetrical uniform emphasizes her disciplined nature. This intentional design approach allows players to understand character traits at a glance. - **Ciel**: Bright personality, warrior attire with big pants and a knife, symbolizing agility and uniqueness. - **Lune**: Cold personality, uniformed look indicating strict adherence to rules. - **Maëlle**: The youngest crew member, her tight pants and classy top showcase her agility and desire for exploration. ## Workflow and File Management I prefer to work on clothing items individually in Marvelous Designer, creating focused files for each garment. For example, I maintain separate files for pants and coats. This method allows me to concentrate on specific details, like patterns and shapes, without cluttering the design process. ### Clothing Library This approach has helped me create a library of clothing assets for all characters. I can easily copy and modify items across different characters, ensuring consistency while allowing for unique designs. ## ZBrush Integration When transitioning to ZBrush, I create a simple base mesh to establish overall proportions before importing it into Marvelous Designer. This helps in fitting and adjusting clothing, allowing for creative freedom to deviate from traditional references to achieve the desired aesthetic. ## Importance of Experimentation I encourage other artists to experiment and not shy away from diverging from references. The most critical aspect is the end result. My experience with Marvelous Designer has been tremendously rewarding; it simplifies the creation of visually appealing clothing rapidly. ## Future Aspirations Expedition 33 holds a special place in my heart as it has significantly influenced my personal growth. My next objective is to enhance my skills in Marvelous Designer and explore tools I have yet to master. I aspire to be a better sculptor and improve my texturing abilities, a goal I set four years ago and continue to pursue fervently. ```
